title: What happens to the median when a bigger value joins?
description: A dot plot has a median of eight, and a new value of eleven is included. The two middle values become eight and eleven, and their average gives the new median. Keeko doubts this and picks the bigger middle value instead.
teaching_notes: One idea: when a value greater than the median joins, the median moves up to the average of the two middle values. Watch for students who pick one of the two middle values instead of averaging them.

source: A data set has median 8 and its two middle values after including 11 are 8 and 11. Find the new median.
video_script.why: A child who knows the median of sorted data sees how it moves when one greater value is included.
video_script.substitution: the book's dot plot with median eight and the included value eleven
video_script.anchor: the dot plot of the book with its median marked
video_script.wrong_move: picks the bigger of the two middle values instead of taking their average
video_script.payoff_line: The new median is nine point five
never_show: 11 as the new median marked as right
maths_rules: included value 11 is greater than the old median 8, so the median rises
check: 9.5 > 8, so the median went up
video_script.design: One dot plot all video. The median marker at eight slides to nine point five. Keeko's wrong idea is the bigger middle value, eleven.
open_questions: The book's dot plot data is not in the extracted text, so the video states only the median eight, the included value eleven and the two middle values.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book, then a dot plot of some data with its median marked at 8 and a new dot waiting at 11

marks.book: the title card From your book appears
marks.plot: the dot plot appears with a marker at 8
marks.new: a new dot at 11 waits beside the plot
marks.ask: a question mark glows over the median marker

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the median.
<bookmark mark='plot'/>Some data is shown as a dot plot, and its median is eight.
<bookmark mark='new'/>A new value, eleven, is then included in the data.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What will the median become?

beats.on_screen: the dot plot and the question stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the sorted dots with equal numbers on both sides of the marker at 8; then the new dot at 11 joins on the right side

marks.mid: the marker at 8 splits the dots into two equal sides
marks.half: the left and right dot counts are shown equal
marks.join: the new dot at 11 slides in on the right
marks.tilt: the right side now holds more dots than the left

narration: <bookmark mark='mid'/>The median is the middle value when the data is sorted.
<bookmark mark='half'/>Before the new value joins, as many dots lie on the left of eight as on the right.
<bookmark mark='join'/>Eleven is greater than eight, so it joins on the right side.
<bookmark mark='tilt'/>Then there are more dots on the right than on the left.

marks.given: the old median and the included value are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the old median is eight, and the value eleven is included.

marks.find: the words the new median are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the new median of the data.

beats.on_screen: 11 > 8, so more values lie above 8 than below it; 8 can no longer be the median

marks.cross: 8 as the median is crossed out

narration: <bookmark mark='greater'/>Step one, compare the new value with the old median. Eleven is greater than eight.
<bookmark mark='cross'/>More values lie above eight than below it, and eight can no longer be the median.

beats.on_screen: the two middle values of the sorted data: 8 and 11

marks.two: the dots at 8 and 11 are circled as the two middle values

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, find the middle of the sorted data. It has two middle values, and they are eight and eleven.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Step three, take the average of the two middle values, because two values share the middle. Eight plus eleven is nineteen.
<bookmark mark='share'/>Nineteen divided by two gives nine point five.

beats.on_screen: check: 9.5 > 8, so the median went up, as expected

marks.check: 9.5 > 8 is written with an up arrow

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Check the result. Nine point five is above eight, so the median went up. That is right when a greater value joins.

marks.ans: the answer is boxed and the median marker slides to 9.5

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The new median is nine point five.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the dot plot
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: median = 11, then the bubble is struck out and 8 and 11 are shown with 9.5 halfway between them

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble shows 11 as the median
marks.fix: the dot at 8 is highlighted as equally in the middle
marks.avg: the bubble is struck out and 9.5 appears halfway between 8 and 11

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the new median is eleven, because eleven is the bigger of the two middle values.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But eight is as much in the middle as eleven is.
<bookmark mark='avg'/>Picking one would leave the other out, so we take the average of both.
